summary:
AstroSense AI is an offline-first predictive health companion designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions. Developed by Team Nano Tech for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, the software addresses the challenge of astronaut medical independence as missions venture farther from Earth and communication delays grow.

The system continuously tracks health data across five core domains—bone and muscle, cardiovascular, immune, behavioral health, and radiation exposure—by comparing each astronaut against their own personal baseline rather than static population averages. Using change-detection algorithms and multi-signal anomaly forecasting, it anticipates health drifts 3 to 7 days before critical thresholds are crossed. Every alert is paired with an explainable plain-language action card drawn from NASA documentation, allowing astronauts and crew medical officers to make informed decisions independently without relying on real-time mission control.

This project is important because early detection prevents costly medical emergencies in isolated environments, while its offline-first and explainable design reduces alert fatigue and offers potential benefits for remote healthcare clinics on Earth.
details:
Benefits & Intended Impact:

  • Empowers crews to spot health changes early and act independently when communication with Earth is delayed or absent (such as a 20-minute one-way delay on Mars missions).
  • Reduces alert fatigue by avoiding population-average false alarms and keeps astronauts in charge as decision-makers rather than relying on automated diagnoses.
    • medical documents to generate plain-language action cards with clear steps.
  • Tools, Technologies, and Architecture:
  • Built to run locally on lightweight, laptop-class computer hardware without needing a cloud link.
  • Designed around NASA's Crew Health and Performance Integrated Data Architecture (CHP-IDA) and Open Science Data Repository (OSDR).
  • Incorporates conceptual supporting layers including nanomaterial-enhanced sweat sensors and palladium-doped tin oxide ($Pd/SnO_{2}$) gas sensors for cabin air monitoring.
  • Prototyped using a random forest model on simulated pipeline data during the initial development phase.
  • Creativity & Design Factors:
  • Focuses on individual baselines rather than static population ranges to catch subtle personal health drifts.
  • Emphasizes explainability and safety by providing uncertainty bands on forecasts and transparent action cards backed by official NASA documentation.
  • Carefully balances advanced predictive technology with strict safety constraints, treating the software strictly as decision-support rather than an unvalidated medical device.
